data.hook: Ten days after clocks fell back, people are still battling exhaustion, wide awake at night yet drained from the day.
data.name: Time Change Fatigue Hits Hard Ten Days Later
data.summary: The end of daylight saving time on November 1 disrupted sleep patterns across the US, leaving many in a loop of daytime tiredness and nighttime restlessness. Users shared frustrations like waking up drained, struggling through long days, and then wasting evenings unable to sleep peacefully. Health experts note this adjustment can fragment sleep for up to two weeks, worsened by shorter days and year-end pressures, making rest the top priority now.

data.name: November Fatigue Hits Hard with Bed-Rotting and Endless Sleep
data.summary: People describe rotting in bed all day, waking up unwell, or fighting the urge to scroll late into the night. This matches CDC data where nearly three-fourths of U.S. adults felt very tired some days in the past three months, and over 15 percent most or all days. Shorter days since Daylight Saving Time ended November 1 disrupt circadian rhythms, while evening phone use delays sleep and cuts rest quality. Many respond with humor, resignation, or a quiet push to protect their peace.
